title: Capitalize the Title
spaceBreakdown:
- string title: modified in place, not newly allocated → O(1) auxiliary
- a few int loop counters → O(1)
- not counted: input/returned string
approach: Scan the string in place, using two indices to mark each word's start and end (delimited by single spaces). For each word, if its length is 1 or 2, lowercase every character; otherwise uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. This is correct because the transformation rule depends only on each word's length, and words are cleanly separated by single spaces with no leading/trailing spaces.
hints: What single property of each word determines whether its first letter should be uppercase or lowercase? The title has no leading/trailing spaces and words are separated by exactly one space.
Use an in-place scan with two indices marking each word's start and end. For "of" (length 2), lowercase both letters; for "tHe" (length 3), uppercase 'T' and lowercase the rest.

```
i = 0
while i < n:
    start = i
    advance i until space or end
    len = i - start
    if len <= 2:
        lowercase title[start..i)
    else:
        uppercase title[start]
        lowercase title[start+1..i)
    skip the space
```

**Single-character word** - word length 1 must stay lowercase
`Input: "i lOve leetcode"` → `Expected: "i Love Leetcode"`
⚠️ Bug: treating length 1 like length ≥3 (uppercase first) → returns "I Love Leetcode"

**Two-character word** - word length 2 must be fully lowercase
`Input: "First leTTeR of EACH Word"` → `Expected: "First Letter of Each Word"`
⚠️ Bug: using `< 2` instead of `<= 2` for the lowercase threshold → returns "First Letter Of Each Word"

**Single word title** - no spaces in the string
`Input: "Leetcode"` → `Expected: "Leetcode"`
⚠️ Bug: only processing words followed by a space, skipping the last word → returns "leetcode"

**All-uppercase word of length ≥3** - must lowercase all but first
`Input: "EACH Word"` → `Expected: "Each Word"`
⚠️ Bug: only uppercasing the first letter without lowercasing the rest → returns "EACH Word"

followUps.q: What if words could be separated by multiple consecutive spaces and you must preserve the exact spacing?
followUps.a: Track runs of spaces separately and copy them through unchanged; only apply the capitalization rule to maximal non-space runs. Time stays O(n), space O(1) if done in place (or O(n) for a new string if spaces are preserved by copying).

followUps.q: What if the title arrives as a streaming input too large to fit in memory, one chunk at a time?
followUps.a: Buffer until you hit a space or chunk boundary, flush each completed word with the rule applied, and carry a partial word across chunk boundaries. Time O(n), space O(maxWordLength) for the buffer.

followUps.q: What if a set of "minor words" (e.g., articles like "of", "the") must stay lowercase even when length ≥3, except the very first word of the title?
followUps.a: After computing each word's transformed form, check membership in the minor-words set; if present and it is not the first word, force it fully lowercase. Time O(n) with an O(1) hash-set lookup per word, space O(k) for the minor-words set of size k.
